metadata.name: CIS Benchmark for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 - Level 1 Server
metadata.description: Center for Internet Security Benchmark for RHEL 9 Level 1 Server Profile
metadata.author: Center for Internet Security

profile.name: CIS Level 1 Server
profile.description: Baseline security configuration for RHEL 9 servers - Level 1 provides practical security without excessive disruption

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of cramfs filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. Disabling unnecessary filesystem types reduces the attack surface.

assessment.detection_step: Verify cramfs kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf with: install cramfs /bin/true

context.rationale: Unused filesystem drivers increase attack surface and should be disabled.

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of freevxfs filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The freevxfs filesystem type is a Veritas filesystem driver that is rarely needed on modern systems.

assessment.detection_step: Verify freevxfs kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/freevxfs.conf with: install freevxfs /bin/true

context.rationale: Removing unused filesystem drivers reduces kernel attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of jffs2 filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The jffs2 filesystem type is used for flash memory devices and is not typically needed on servers.

assessment.detection_step: Verify jffs2 kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/jffs2.conf with: install jffs2 /bin/true

context.rationale: Unused filesystem drivers should be disabled to reduce attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of hfs filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The hfs filesystem type is the Apple Macintosh filesystem and is not needed on Linux servers.

assessment.detection_step: Verify hfs kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/hfs.conf with: install hfs /bin/true

context.rationale: Disabling unused filesystem types reduces attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of hfsplus filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The hfsplus filesystem is the extended Apple Macintosh filesystem.

assessment.detection_step: Verify hfsplus kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/hfsplus.conf with: install hfsplus /bin/true

context.rationale: Removing unused filesystem drivers reduces kernel attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of squashfs filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The squashfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only filesystem used for embedded systems.

assessment.detection_step: Verify squashfs kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/squashfs.conf with: install squashfs /bin/true
remediation.service_impact: May affect live CD/snap package functionality

context.rationale: Disabling unused filesystem types reduces attack surface.
context.impact: Low - May affect some container/snap functionality

rules.rule_name: Ensure mounting of udf filesystems is disabled
rules.rule_description: The udf filesystem type is the Universal Disk Format used for optical media.

assessment.detection_step: Verify udf kernel module is disabled

remediation.remediation_step: Create or edit /etc/modprobe.d/udf.conf with: install udf /bin/true

context.rationale: Removing unused filesystem drivers reduces kernel attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure /tmp is configured
rules.rule_description: The /tmp directory is a world-writable directory used for temporary files. It should be configured as a separate filesystem with appropriate mount options.

assessment.detection_step: Verify /tmp is a separate mount point
assessment.expected_value: /tmp on /tmp type tmpfs or separate partition

remediation.remediation_step: Configure /tmp as tmpfs or separate partition in /etc/fstab with nodev,nosuid,noexec options

context.rationale: Separate /tmp prevents resource exhaustion and allows restrictive mount options.

rules.rule_name: Ensure nodev option set on /tmp partition
rules.rule_description: The nodev mount option specifies that the filesystem cannot contain special device files.

remediation.remediation_step: Add nodev option to /tmp in /etc/fstab

context.rationale: Prevents creation of device files in /tmp which could be used for attacks.

rules.rule_name: Ensure nosuid option set on /tmp partition
rules.rule_description: The nosuid mount option prevents set-user-identifier and set-group-identifier bits from taking effect.

remediation.remediation_step: Add nosuid option to /tmp in /etc/fstab

context.rationale: Prevents privilege escalation via SUID binaries in /tmp.

rules.rule_name: Ensure noexec option set on /tmp partition
rules.rule_description: The noexec mount option prevents direct execution of binaries from the filesystem.

remediation.remediation_step: Add noexec option to /tmp in /etc/fstab
remediation.service_impact: May affect some scripts that execute from /tmp

context.rationale: Prevents execution of malicious binaries from /tmp.

rules.rule_name: Ensure package manager repositories are configured
rules.rule_description: Systems need to have package manager repositories configured to ensure they receive security updates.

assessment.detection_step: Verify repositories are configured and accessible

remediation.remediation_step: Configure appropriate package repositories using subscription-manager or by adding repo files

context.rationale: Configured repositories are essential for receiving security updates.

rules.rule_name: Ensure GPG keys are configured
rules.rule_description: GPG keys are used to verify the authenticity of packages during installation.

assessment.detection_step: Verify Red Hat GPG keys are installed

remediation.remediation_step: Import Red Hat GPG keys: rpm --import /etc/pki/rpm-gpg/RPM-GPG-KEY-redhat-release

context.rationale: GPG keys ensure package authenticity and integrity.
context.impact: High - Prevents installation of tampered packages

rules.rule_name: Ensure AIDE is installed
rules.rule_description: Advanced Intrusion Detection Environment (AIDE) provides file integrity checking.

remediation.remediation_step: Install AIDE: dnf install aide && aide --init && mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new.gz /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz
remediation.service_impact: Initial database creation may take time

context.rationale: File integrity monitoring detects unauthorized file changes.

rules.rule_name: Ensure bootloader password is set
rules.rule_description: Setting the bootloader password protects against unauthorized changes to boot parameters.

remediation.remediation_step: Set GRUB password: grub2-setpassword && grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg

context.rationale: Bootloader password prevents unauthorized modification of boot parameters.

rules.rule_name: Ensure core dumps are restricted
rules.rule_description: Core dumps can contain sensitive information and should be restricted.

remediation.remediation_step: Add to /etc/security/limits.conf: * hard core 0
remediation.service_impact: Core dumps disabled for new sessions

context.rationale: Core dumps may contain sensitive memory data and consume disk space.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SELinux is installed
rules.rule_description: SELinux provides mandatory access control for enhanced security.

remediation.remediation_step: Install SELinux packages: dnf install libselinux selinux-policy-targeted

context.rationale: SELinux provides critical mandatory access control capabilities.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SELinux is not disabled in bootloader configuration
rules.rule_description: SELinux should not be disabled via bootloader parameters.

assessment.detection_step: Verify SELinux is not disabled in GRUB
assessment.expected_value: No output (selinux=0 should not be present)

remediation.remediation_step: Remove selinux=0 from kernel parameters: grubby --update-kernel=ALL --remove-args='selinux=0'
remediation.service_impact: SELinux will be enabled after reboot

context.rationale: Disabling SELinux at boot removes a critical security control.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SELinux policy is configured
rules.rule_description: SELinux should be configured with an appropriate policy.

remediation.remediation_step: Edit /etc/selinux/config: SELINUXTYPE=targeted

context.rationale: Targeted policy provides security for specific services while allowing normal operation.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SELinux mode is enforcing or permissive
rules.rule_description: SELinux should be running in enforcing mode for maximum security.

remediation.remediation_step: Set SELinux to enforcing: Edit /etc/selinux/config: SELINUX=enforcing

context.rationale: Enforcing mode actively blocks policy violations.

rules.rule_name: Ensure cron daemon is enabled and running
rules.rule_description: The cron daemon is used to execute scheduled jobs and must be running.

assessment.detection_step: Verify crond service is enabled and running
assessment.check_command: systemctl is-enabled crond && systemctl is-active crond

remediation.remediation_step: Enable and start crond: systemctl enable --now crond

context.rationale: Cron is essential for scheduled system maintenance tasks.

rules.rule_name: Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured
rules.rule_description: The SSH configuration file must have proper permissions.

remediation.remediation_step: Set proper permissions: chmod 600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config && chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config

context.rationale: Protecting SSH config prevents unauthorized modifications.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH access is limited
rules.rule_description: SSH access should be limited to specific users or groups.

assessment.detection_step: Verify SSH access restrictions are configured
assessment.expected_value: At least one access control directive should be configured

remediation.remediation_step: Add AllowUsers or AllowGroups directive to /etc/ssh/sshd_config

context.rationale: Limiting SSH access reduces the attack surface for remote access.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH LogLevel is appropriate
rules.rule_description: SSH should be configured to log at VERBOSE or INFO level for security monitoring.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: LogLevel VERBOSE

context.rationale: Verbose logging helps detect and investigate security incidents.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH X11 forwarding is disabled
rules.rule_description: X11 forwarding should be disabled unless specifically required.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: X11Forwarding no

context.rationale: X11 forwarding can be used for attacks and increases attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH MaxAuthTries is set to 4 or less
rules.rule_description: The MaxAuthTries parameter limits the number of authentication attempts per connection.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: MaxAuthTries 4

context.rationale: Limiting auth attempts mitigates brute force attacks.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH IgnoreRhosts is enabled
rules.rule_description: The .rhosts and .shosts files should not be used for authentication.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: IgnoreRhosts yes

context.rationale: Rhosts authentication is insecure and should be disabled.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH HostbasedAuthentication is disabled
rules.rule_description: Host-based authentication should be disabled as it is insecure.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: HostbasedAuthentication no

context.rationale: Host-based authentication can be spoofed and is not secure.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH root login is disabled
rules.rule_description: Direct root login via SSH should be disabled.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: PermitRootLogin no

context.rationale: Preventing direct root login improves accountability and reduces attack surface.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled
rules.rule_description: Empty passwords must not be permitted for SSH authentication.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: PermitEmptyPasswords no

context.rationale: Empty passwords provide no authentication security.

rules.rule_name: Ensure SSH PermitUserEnvironment is disabled
rules.rule_description: User environment should not be enabled in SSH.

remediation.remediation_step: Add or modify in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: PermitUserEnvironment no

context.rationale: User environment can bypass security controls.

rules.rule_name: Ensure password creation requirements are configured
rules.rule_description: Strong password requirements should be enforced.

assessment.expected_value: minlen = 14 or more, minclass = 4 or appropriate credit settings

remediation.remediation_step: Configure /etc/security/pwquality.conf with strong password requirements

context.rationale: Strong passwords are essential for authentication security.

rules.rule_name: Ensure password expiration is configured
rules.rule_description: Password expiration should be configured appropriately.

remediation.remediation_step: Configure /etc/login.defs with appropriate expiration settings

context.rationale: Password expiration limits the window of opportunity for compromised credentials.

rules.rule_name: Ensure default user shell timeout is configured
rules.rule_description: Inactive sessions should be automatically terminated.

remediation.remediation_step: Add to /etc/profile.d/tmout.sh: TMOUT=900; export TMOUT

context.rationale: Automatic session timeout prevents unauthorized access to unattended sessions.

rules.rule_name: Ensure permissions on /etc/passwd are configured
rules.rule_description: The /etc/passwd file must have proper permissions.

remediation.remediation_step: chmod 644 /etc/passwd && chown root:root /etc/passwd

context.rationale: Proper permissions prevent unauthorized modification of user accounts.

rules.rule_name: Ensure permissions on /etc/shadow are configured
rules.rule_description: The /etc/shadow file must have restrictive permissions.

remediation.remediation_step: chmod 0000 /etc/shadow && chown root:root /etc/shadow

context.rationale: Shadow file contains password hashes and must be protected.

rules.rule_name: Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords
rules.rule_description: All accounts must use shadowed passwords.

remediation.remediation_step: Convert accounts to use shadowed passwords: pwconv

context.rationale: Shadowed passwords protect password hashes from being accessible.

rules.rule_name: Ensure root is the only UID 0 account
rules.rule_description: Only the root account should have UID 0.

remediation.remediation_step: Change UID of non-root accounts with UID 0 or remove them

context.rationale: Multiple UID 0 accounts complicate audit and increase attack surface.
